scope: Comparison between ANN and RSM outputs

matched: Figure 8 compares laboratory data with modeling results of ANN and RSM
ANN outputs in Fig. 8a show superior predictive capability, especially initial stages for Ammonia Nitrogen concentration and removal efficiency based on pH
Figure 8b displays Phosphate concentration and removal efficiency based on pH; both models show strong predictive abilities except middle deviated point
Figure 8c displays Ammonia Nitrogen based on TOC; ANN excellent at all points while RSM struggled at initial points
Figure 8d displays Phosphate based on TOC; ANN demonstrated superior accuracy representing the data
Microalgae photosynthetic activity markedly elevates pH; continuous bioreactor pH observed lower than sequencing batch photoreactor, favoring growth
Optimal pH values vary across microalgae; Chlorella in photobioreactor with dairy effluent maximized at pH 6.3–7.5
Quantitative assessment via Table 3 shows ANN consistently outperformed RSM across all response variables
For Ammonia Nitrogen, ANN achieved RMSE = 0.189 and MAE = 0.142 (approx 41% error reduction compared to RSM RMSE = 0.324, MAE = 0.281)
Residual error distribution histogram in Fig. 9 shows ANN errors normally distributed and sharply peaked around zero
RSM error distribution exhibits wider spread and higher standard deviation, showing quadratic polynomial equations struggle with complex non-linear biological fluctuations
Statistical and visual evidence confirms ANN provides superior approximation of MBR system behavior
